newsitem.title: GERMANY: German SPD leader rejects Kohl tax demands.
newsitem.headline: German SPD leader rejects Kohl tax demands.

text.p: Oskar Lafontaine, leader of Germany's opposition Social Democrats, on Tuesday rejected conditions set by Chancellor Helmut Kohl for achieving a compromise deal on reforming the German tax system.
Replying to a open letter from Kohl, Lafontaine said the German leader's insistence on agreeing tax cuts before working out how to pay for them "cannot be held to".

Lafontaine repeated his demand to agree cuts in Germany's occupational insurance schemes before moving on to the tax reforms, and called for the government to clarify how it planned to finance its planned tax cuts.

The SPD says the coalition government's tax cutting plans would open up a 56 billion mark hole in state finances -- while Finance Minister Theo Waigel says the net tax cuts would total up to 30 billion marks.

Lafontaine said it was possible at the talks to agree to cut labour insurances charges from July, to slash the bottom rate of income tax, to increase child allowances and to cut the main corporate tax rate.
The two sides were due to meet on Wednesday morning, but on Tuesday afternoon there was still uncertainty over where and whether the talks would take place.
Government spokesman Peter Hausmann said he expected the talks to start at 9 a.m. (0700 GMT) in the federal chancellery.
